title: Preamble to the Constitution of India
source: Constitution of India, Preamble

title: Name and territory of the Union
content:
Article 1: Name and territory of the Union
(1) India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
(2) The States and the territories thereof shall be as specified in the First Schedule.
(3) The territory of India shall comprise the territories of the States, the Union territories specified in the First Schedule, and such other territories as may be acquired.
part: PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY
source: Constitution of India, PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY, Article 1
keywords: name and territory of the union

title: Admission or establishment of new States
content:
Article 2: Admission or establishment of new States
Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
part: PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY
source: Constitution of India, PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY, Article 2
keywords: admission or establishment of new states

title: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
content:
Article 3: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
Parliament may by law form a new State by separation of territory from any State or by uniting two or more States or parts of States, increase the area of any State, diminish the area of any State, alter the boundaries of any State, and alter the name of any State, subject to Presidential recommendation and reference to affected State Legislatures.
part: PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY
source: Constitution of India, PART I: THE UNION AND ITS TERRITORY, Article 3
keywords: formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states

title: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
content:
Article 5: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
At the commencement of this Constitution, every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and who was born in the territory of India, or either of whose parents was born in the territory of India, or who has been ordinarily resident in the territory of India for not less than five years immediately preceding such commencement, shall be a citizen of India.
source: Constitution of India, PART II: CITIZENSHIP, Article 5
keywords: citizenship at the commencement of the constitution

title: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens.
content:
Article 9: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens.
No person shall be a citizen of India by virtue of article 5, or be deemed to be a citizen of India, if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign State. Single citizenship is a fundamental pillar of the Indian constitutional structure.
source: Constitution of India, PART II: CITIZENSHIP, Article 9
keywords: persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign state not to be citizens.

title: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
content:
Article 11: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
Parliament has sovereign power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship, pursuant to which the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted.
source: Constitution of India, PART II: CITIZENSHIP, Article 11
keywords: parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law

title: Definition of State
content:
Article 12: Definition of State
In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, "the State" includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 12

title: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights
content:
Article 13: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights
(1) All laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
(2) The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the rights conferred by this Part and any law made in contravention of this clause shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void (Doctrine of Judicial Review).

Right to Equality
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 13
keywords: laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights

title: Equality before law
content:
Article 14: Equality before law
The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
Explanation: Article 14 strikes at arbitrariness in state action and ensures that equals are treated equally while permitting reasonable classification having an intelligible differentia and a rational nexus to the statutory objective sought to be achieved.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 14

title: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
content:
Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
(1) The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.
(2) No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction or condition with regard to access to shops, public restaurants, hotels and places of public entertainment, or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds.
(3) Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making any special provision for women and children.
(4) Special provisions permitted for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
(5) Special provisions for admission to educational institutions, including private institutions.
(6) Special provisions and reservation up to 10% for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 15
keywords: prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth

title: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
content:
Article 16: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
(1) There shall be equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
(2) No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them, be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the State.
(4) State empowered to make reservations for any backward class of citizens not adequately represented in the services under the State.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 16
keywords: equality of opportunity in matters of public employment

title: Abolition of Untouchability
content:
Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability
"Untouchability" is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of "Untouchability" shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law (Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955).
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 17

title: Abolition of titles
content:
Article 18: Abolition of titles
No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State. No citizen of India shall accept any title from any foreign State.

Right to Freedom
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 18

title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 19
keywords: protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.

title: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
content:
Article 20: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
(1) No ex-post facto law: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence.
(2) No double jeopardy: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
(3) No self-incrimination: No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 20
keywords: protection in respect of conviction for offences

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
content:
Article 21: Protection of life and personal liberty
No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
Explanation: Article 21 is the heart and cornerstone of fundamental rights under . As interpreted expansively by the Supreme Court in Maneka Gandhi, Francis Coralie, and K.S. Puttaswamy:
- Life does not mean mere animal existence; it encompasses the right to live with human dignity.
- The 'procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable, incorporating the principles of natural justice and procedural due process.
- Substantive rights evolved under Article 21 include:
* Right to Privacy (declared a fundamental right in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017)
* Right to clean environment, clean air and water
* Right to speedy trial and legal aid
* Right to health and medical assistance
* Right to livelihood
* Right to shelter and sleep
* Right against solitary confinement and custodial torture
* Right to dignity of women and protection against sexual harassment.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 21
keywords: protection of life and personal liberty

title: Right to education
content:
Article 21A: Right to education
The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine. Enacted pursuant to the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 21A

title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
content:
Article 22: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
(1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice.
(2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest excluding journey time, and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.
(4) Preventive detention safeguards and Advisory Board requirements.

Right against Exploitation
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 22
keywords: protection against arrest and detention in certain cases

title: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
content:
Article 23: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 23
keywords: prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour

title: Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
content:
Article 24: Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.

Right to Freedom of Religion
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 24
keywords: prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.

title: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
content:
Article 25: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
(1) Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion.
(2) The State is empowered to regulate economic, financial, political or other secular activities associated with religious practice, and provide for social welfare and reform.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 25
keywords: freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion

title: Freedom to manage religious affairs
content:
Article 26: Freedom to manage religious affairs
Subject to public order, morality and health, every religious denomination or any section thereof shall have the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and to own, acquire and administer property.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 26

title: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
content:
Article 27: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
No person shall be compelled to pay any taxes, the proceeds of which are specifically appropriated in payment of expenses for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 27
keywords: freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion

title: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.
content:
Article 28: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.
Cultural and Educational Rights
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 28
keywords: freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.

title: Protection of interests of minorities
content:
Article 29: Protection of interests of minorities
(1) Any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
(2) No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language or any of them.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 29

title: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
content:
Article 30: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
(1) All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

Right to Constitutional Remedies
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 30
keywords: right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
content:
Article 32: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
(1) The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.
(2) The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, whichever may be appropriate, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by this Part.
Explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the "very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it".
Types of Constitutional Writs:
- Habeas Corpus: "To have the body". Issued to secure the release of a person unlawfully or illegally detained in custody.
- Mandamus: "We command". Issued to compel a public official, tribunal, or lower body to perform a mandatory statutory or public duty.
- Prohibition: Issued by a superior court to prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its territorial or statutory jurisdiction.
- Certiorari: "To be certified". Issued to quash the order or decision of an inferior court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial body on grounds of lack of jurisdiction, excess of jurisdiction, or violation of principles of natural justice.
- Quo Warranto: "By what authority". Issued to challenge the legal authority of a person holding a substantive public office without lawful title.
source: Constitution of India, PART III: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Article 32
keywords: remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this part

title: Application of the principles contained in this Part
content:
Article 37: Application of the principles contained in this Part
The provisions contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 37
keywords: application of the principles contained in this part

title: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
content:
Article 39: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
Adequate means of livelihood, distribution of material resources to subserve common good, prevention of concentration of wealth, equal pay for equal work for both men and women, protection of health of workers and children.
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 39
keywords: certain principles of policy to be followed by the state

title: Equal justice and free legal aid
content:
Article 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid
The State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice, on a basis of equal opportunity, and shall, in particular, provide free legal aid, by suitable legislation or schemes or in any other way, to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. (Foundation of Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 / DLSA / NALSA).
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 39A
keywords: equal justice and free legal aid

title: Organisation of village panchayats
content:
Article 40: Organisation of village panchayats
The State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government. (Realised through 73rd Amendment).
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 40

title: Uniform civil code for the citizens
content:
Article 44: Uniform civil code for the citizens
The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 44
keywords: uniform civil code for the citizens

title: Separation of judiciary from executive
content:
Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive
The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.
part: PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY
source: Constitution of India, PART IV: DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY, Article 50

title: Fundamental duties
source: Constitution of India, PART IVA: FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES, Article 51A

title: The President of India
content:
Article 52: The President of India
There shall be a President of India.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 52

title: Executive power of the Union
content:
Article 53: Executive power of the Union
The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 53

title: Power of President to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases
content:
Article 72: Power of President to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases
The President shall have the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence in all cases where the punishment is by a Court Martial, in all cases where the punishment is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, and in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 72
keywords: power of president to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases

title: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
content:
Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 74
keywords: council of ministers to aid and advise president

title: Other provisions as to Ministers
content:
Article 75: Other provisions as to Ministers
The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 75

title: Attorney-General for India
content:
Article 76: Attorney-General for India
The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney-General for India.

The Union Judiciary / Supreme Court
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 76

title: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
content:
Article 124: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and other Judges.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 124
keywords: establishment and constitution of supreme court

title: Supreme Court to be a court of record
content:
Article 129: Supreme Court to be a court of record
The Supreme Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 129
keywords: supreme court to be a court of record

title: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
content:
Article 131: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the Supreme Court shall, to the exclusion of any other court, have original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States, or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more other States on the other, or between two or more States.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 131
keywords: original jurisdiction of the supreme court

title: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
content:
Article 136: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
Notwithstanding anything in this Chapter, the Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 136
keywords: special leave to appeal by the supreme court

title: Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts
content:
Article 141: Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts
The law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India (Principle of Stare Decisis).
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 141
keywords: law declared by supreme court to be binding on all courts

title: Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
content:
Article 142: Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
source: Constitution of India, PART V: THE UNION, Article 142
keywords: enforcement of decrees and orders of supreme court and orders as to discovery, etc.

title: Governors of States
content:
Article 153: Governors of States
There shall be a Governor for each State.
source: Constitution of India, PART VI: THE STATES, Article 153

title: High Courts for States
content:
Article 214: High Courts for States
There shall be a High Court for each State.
source: Constitution of India, PART VI: THE STATES, Article 214

title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
content:
Article 226: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
(1) Notwithstanding anything in article 32, every High Court shall have power, throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government, within those territories directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them:
(a) for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III; and
(b) for any other purpose.
Explanation: The writ jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 226 is broader in scope than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32, because High Courts can issue writs not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also "for any other purpose" (enforcement of ordinary statutory or legal rights).
source: Constitution of India, PART VI: THE STATES, Article 226
keywords: power of high courts to issue certain writs

title: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
content:
Article 300A: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. (Right to Property is a Constitutional and Human Right, transformed from a Fundamental Right by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978).
part: PART XII: FINANCE, PROPERTY, CONTRACTS AND SUITS
source: Constitution of India, PART XII: FINANCE, PROPERTY, CONTRACTS AND SUITS, Article 300A
keywords: persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law

title: Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State.
content:
Article 311: Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State.
Provides constitutional safeguards against arbitrary dismissal without reasonable opportunity of showing cause against the action proposed.
part: PART XIV: SERVICES UNDER THE UNION AND THE STATES
source: Constitution of India, PART XIV: SERVICES UNDER THE UNION AND THE STATES, Article 311
keywords: dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the union or a state.

title: Official language of the Union
content:
Article 343: Official language of the Union
The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script. The international form of Indian numerals shall be used.
source: Constitution of India, PART XVII: OFFICIAL LANGUAGE, Article 343

title: Proclamation of Emergency (National Emergency)
content:
Article 352: Proclamation of Emergency (National Emergency)
If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion, he may, by Proclamation, make a declaration of Emergency.
source: Constitution of India, PART XVIII: EMERGENCY PROVISIONS, Article 352

title: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States (President's Rule / State Emergency)
content:
Article 356: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States (President's Rule / State Emergency)
If the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor of a State or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution, the President may proclaim State Emergency.
ARTICLE 358 & 359: Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies, and suspension of enforcement of rights conferred by Part III (except Articles 20 and 21 which can never be suspended even during an emergency).
source: Constitution of India, PART XVIII: EMERGENCY PROVISIONS, Article 356
keywords: provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in states (president's rule / state emergency)

title: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
content:
Article 368: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.
Amendments require a special majority (majority of the total membership of each House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting). Amendments affecting federal provisions require ratification by legislatures of not less than one-half of the States.
Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, 1973): Parliament cannot alter, destroy or abrogate the Basic Structure or essential framework of .

SCHEDULES TO FIRST SCHEDULE: Names of the 28 States and 8 Union Territories and their territorial extents.
SECOND SCHEDULE: Provisions as to the President, Governors, Speaker, Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
THIRD SCHEDULE: Forms of Oaths or Affirmations for Ministers, Judges, MPs, MLAs, and constitutional authorities.
FOURTH SCHEDULE: Allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to the States and Union Territories.
FIFTH SCHEDULE: Provisions as to the Administration and Control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
SIXTH SCHEDULE: Provisions as to the Administration of Tribal Areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (Autonomous District Councils).
SEVENTH SCHEDULE: The Three Legislative Lists:
- List I (Union List): 100 subjects under exclusive parliamentary jurisdiction (Defence, Foreign Affairs, Atomic Energy, Banking, Railways, Airways, Citizenship).
- List II (State List): 61 subjects under exclusive State legislative jurisdiction (Public order, Police, Public health, Agriculture, Local government, Prisons).
- List III (Concurrent List): 52 subjects where both Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws, with Union law prevailing in case of conflict (Criminal law, Criminal procedure, Marriage and divorce, Education, Forests, Trade unions).
EIGHTH SCHEDULE: The 22 Officially Recognized Languages of India: Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santhali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu.
NINTH SCHEDULE: Acts and Regulations protected from judicial scrutiny under Article 31B (subject to Basic Structure review for laws added after April 24, 1973 under I.R. Coelho case).
TENTH SCHEDULE: Anti-Defection Law: Disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection from their political party (Added by 52nd Amendment Act, 1985).
ELEVENTH SCHEDULE: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (Contains 29 functional matters added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992).
TWELFTH SCHEDULE: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities (Contains 18 urban functional matters added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992).
part: PART XX: AMENDMENT OF THE CONSTITUTION
source: Constitution of India, PART XX: AMENDMENT OF THE CONSTITUTION, Article 368
keywords: power of parliament to amend the constitution and procedure therefor
